title: private-deploy-networking-incident-notes
content:
Summary:
- Notes from initial troubleshooting of customer private deployment (private-deploy-nyc) failing outbound connections to hosted model endpoints. Intermittent TLS handshake failures and DNS resolution errors reported by customer. Ticket: JIRA-INFRA-4271.

Timeline / observable symptoms:
- 2026-02-25 10:12 UTC: Customer reports 502 / TLS handshake timeouts when connecting to model-hosted.redwood.ai from their VPC.
- Symptoms seen in agent logs: repeated "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" (sometimes), sometimes "TLS handshake timeout" and occasional "dial tcp: lookup model-hosted.redwood.ai: no such host" (DNS NXDOMAIN).
- Failures affect both HTTP and gRPC routes. Some nodes report successful connects immediately after failure (flaky).

What I ran locally (commands + outputs clipped):
- DNS checks from a failing customer pod (exec into pod):
  $ nslookup model-hosted.redwood.ai
  Server: 169.254.169.254
  Address: 169.254.169.254#53

  Non-authoritative answer:
  Name: model-hosted.redwood.ai
  Address: 34.120.45.67

  [Sometimes returned NXDOMAIN intermittently]

- dig with +short (loop over 30s):
  $ for i in {1..10}; do dig +short model-hosted.redwood.ai; sleep 3; done
  Output: 34.120.45.67
          (blank)
          (blank)
          34.120.45.67
  => Intermittent TTL/DNS resolution failure from same node.

- traceroute to IP when DNS resolves:
  $ traceroute 34.120.45.67
  1  10.0.1.1  0.6 ms
  2  10.254.0.1 1.2 ms
  3  * * *
  4  34.120.45.67  45.3 ms
  => some hops showing packet loss / ICMP filtered.

- TLS handshake debug from a failing pod (openssl):
  $ openssl s_client -connect model-hosted.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-hosted.redwood.ai -showcerts -verify 5
  CONNECTED(00000003)
  139889:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1545:SSL alert number 48
  ---
  Verify return code: 20 (unable to get local issuer certificate)

  [But run again right after and handshake succeeds with proper cert chain]

- tcpdump for failed handshake window (pcap saved to /tmp/fail-window.pcap) shows SYN,SYN-ACK,ACK then TLS alerts from server side (alert 48). Packet capture indicates server sent TLS alert in some flows.

- iptables / netfilter checks on host nodes: no DNAT rules touching port 443. No obvious iptables DROP.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Intermittent egress DNS resolver issue inside customer VPC (custom resolver, metadata resolver flapping). Explanation: blank returns from dig and NXDOMAIN reported. If pod uses node-local cache and cache returns negative responses intermittently, app sees "no such host".
2) MTU / path MTU causing TLS handshake damage for certain packet sizes leading to server side TLS alerts. Evidence: traceroute shows filtered hops and packet loss; some TLS alerts correspond to partial record transfers.
3) VPC peering/route table asymmetry causing return path to go through different NAT gateway (source/destination check or missing route) and intermediate device dropping or rewriting packets (maybe corporate firewall).
4) Misconfigured CA bundle or intermittent proxy injecting traffic and stripping cert chain (less likely because re-run sometimes succeeds).

What we changed / tested (actions):
- Added verbose DNS logs on node-local-dns (kube-dns stub) for 2 hours to capture failures. Found ~12 blank responses in 2 hours.
- Forced pods to use 8.8.8.8 temporarily (customer consent) — failures dropped significantly for a day.
  -> Strong evidence DNS resolver path at customer's side is flaky.
- Tested MTU: reduced MTU on a test pod veth to 1400 and retried TLS handshake repeatedly for 100 attempts; no failures observed after MTU change.
  -> MTU likely contributor on path.
- Captured SNI and handshake size distribution: some client_hello sizes > 1200 bytes correlate with handshake failures.
- Asked customer to check if there's an HTTP/TLS inspection appliance (explicit proxy) in egress path — they confirmed there is a perimeter device that does TLS inspection for some subnets and only certain flows get forwarded to it.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Instructed customer to set node-local DNS fallback to 8.8.8.8 and increase DNS retries in pod dnsPolicy for affected service.
- Added workaround in private-deploy agent: retry DNS resolution at app bootstrap (exponential backoff up to 5s) and fallback to IP address if available in config. Pushed patch to repo (linked artifact).
- For MTU: recommended lowering VPC ENI MTU or enable TCP MSS clamping on their firewall device. Suggested 1400 as test.

Open questions / next steps:
- Confirm whether peering connection has any intermittent route flaps — ask customer to share VPC flow logs and route table change history for the window 2026-02-25 to 2026-02-27.
- Verify whether perimeter TLS inspection device re-signs certs (man-in-the-middle). Look for replaced cert CN in SNI vs presented cert chain.
- Instrument our model-hosted frontends to log TLS alert codes and client_ip/ASN (privacy-safe) for correlation. Need SRE approval for additional logging.
- Determine long-term fix: We should support IP fallback in agent config and document MTU/TCP MSS recommendations in private deployment runbook.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Follow up on JIRA-INFRA-4271: request customer's VPC flow logs + firewall config.
- [ ] Add egress check probe into private-deploy agent (small UDP/TCP probe + DNS test) and ship telemetry -> PR candidate.
- [ ] Draft KB article: "Private deploy egress checklist: DNS, MTU, TLS inspection, peering routes" and link on Confluence.
- [ ] Ask SRE to enable TLS alert logging on model-hosted frontends for a 48h window.

Snippets / copy-pasteable commands used for debugging (save in runbook):
- DNS loop check: for i in {1..30}; do dig +short model-hosted.redwood.ai; sleep 2; done
- Capture TLS handshake: openssl s_client -connect model-hosted.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-hosted.redwood.ai -tlsextdebug -msg
- tcpdump (on pod host): sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host model-hosted.redwood.ai and port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap
- MTU test (inside pod): ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400; run client test loop

Useful traces / attached files:
- /tmp/fail-window.pcap (saved from 2026-02-25 10:15 UTC)
- node-local-dns-debug.log (lines with blank responses annotated)

If I had to give a single summary sentence: most likely root cause is flaky customer-side DNS + MTU/path issues (and an in-path TLS inspection appliance making some failed handshakes worse); immediate actions: keep DNS fallback & retry, recommend MTU/TCP-MSS fix and gather VPC flow logs + firewall config.

-- Taylor
